hints: Negative numbers mean a window sum can rise or fall, so a two-pointer rule is unsafe.
Let prefix[i] be the sum before index i; a subarray ending here has sum x when an earlier prefix equals currentPrefix-x.
Store how often each prefix sum has appeared, including prefix 0 once.
analogy: For each stopping point, look for an earlier balance that is exactly x less.
algorithm: At each element update prefix, add frequency[prefix-x] to the count, then increment frequency[prefix]. Use a wide integer for counts and sums.
correctness: A subarray sum is the difference of its ending and preceding prefix sums; frequency counts every valid preceding boundary exactly once.
complexity: O(n) expected time and O(n) space.
example: For [2,-1,3,5,-2] and x=7, the whole array sums to 7, so it contributes one subarray. The other contiguous ranges do not sum to 7.
